lesson: Schema-drift early-warning: after any refactor that consolidates or renames staging columns, run `SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema='stage' AND table_name=<refactored_table>` against BOTH the dev DB (where the refactor lives) and the prod DB (pre-deploy state). Any column present in dev's .yml but missing from prod's relation = an `--full-refresh` will be required on first deploy.

lesson: NRR/GRR acquisition-cohort policy (per Svet, FY26-Q4): customers must have lived ≥ 4 full quarters before they enter the retention cohort (`wd_customer_lifetime_qtr > 4`, NOT `>= 4`). The `>= 4` form pulls in customers acquired DURING the NRR window — ~90-92% of their EoP balance is Net New (brand-new logos / new account×product tuples), inflating FY26-Q4 incremental from the correct $524M to $588.7M. Reverted in PR #443 (qa) / #444 (prod).

When validating NRR/GRR against PROD, compare BoP + EoP + Incremental for EACH T4Q-ending quarter (5+ recent quarters), not just the headline NRR/GRR %. Incremental = EoP – BoP – Churn + Expansion is the most discrepancy-revealing column. PR #444 validation table format: T4Q-ending | BoP | EoP | Incremental | NRR% | GRR%.

Acquisition cohort fix in PR #466 (EDAEM-2183): advance `acq_fiscal_quarter_name` (+ begin/end dates) by EXACTLY one fiscal quarter in the acq CTE of arr_product_customer_retention_dashboard + arr_product_customer_retention_incrementals_dashboard. Reason: acquisition cohort should be excluded from NRR/GRR for FOUR FULL QUARTERS post-acquisition; the off-by-one quarter shift ensures the cohort exits exclusion at the right quarter boundary.

For NRR/GRR-style validation, prefer SINGULAR dbt tests (e.g. `test_nrr_grr_acquisition_cohort`) over UNIT tests. Unit tests are a poor fit because: (1) they require fixture maintenance as the acquisition file grows; (2) they cannot mock wd_date or current_date(), which are used in the max_fy CTE — making the rr_start/rr_end window fan-out fragile. Pattern from PR #466.

lesson: ARR shown in the 'Partnerships' segment is driven by PARTNER_TYPE, not by IS_STRATEGIC_PARTNER or BUSINESS_SEGMENT. PARTNER_TYPE is set in stg_em_int_agree_strategic_partner: 'Strategic Partner' when is_strategic_partner=TRUE, else 'Channel Partner' when opportunity_segment='Partners', else 'Innovation Partner' when partner_track='Innovation'. Innovation/Channel-partner lines have is_strategic_partner=FALSE and business_segment=NULL (the region UDF returns NULL). Consequence: updating the strategic-partner seed/gsheet (REF_/LKP_STRATEGIC_PARTNERS) does NOT move Innovation/Channel-partner ARR out of Partnerships -- that lever only affects is_strategic_partner -> business_segment. Verified on Proquire Plus Inc.: ~$63k = two Innovation Partner agreements (a1XVT00000Bn8PV2AZ $33,001.81 + a1XVT00000CKQVh2AP $29,940.00) on 'Connect Platinum Tier Fees' via partner_track='Innovation'; plus $30k Channel Partner (a1XVT00000Dxkwz2AB, opportunity_segment='Partners'). Values tie penny-for-penny finance_line_analytics -> arr_line_categories -> arr_product_categories (as_was_date 2026-07-04, FY27-Q2 End Balance). Note: 'Partnerships' has no literal in the dbt repo -- the label is applied in the Sigma/BI layer on top of PARTNER_TYPE.
evidence: Live finance_prod validation 2026-07-05/07 for Proquire NRR/segment question (Svetlana Artamonova, #arr_analytics_super_user_group). Source: stg_em_int_agree_strategic_partner partner_type case; udf_get_business_segment.

lesson: Always aggregate ARR on split_arr_usd_current, never a raw ARR column. Split/partner deals double-count otherwise (root cause of a reported ~$15M churn 'variance').

lesson: NRR Begin Balance identity: NRR BB for quarter Q must equal Ending ARR of Q-4 (trailing-4-quarter), excluding M&A (Sana/Paradox). Use this as the first NRR tie-out; a break means BoP/EoP is pulling the wrong balance.
evidence: Svet 5/12 hard rule; ARR Policy doc is source of truth. #arr_analytics_super_user_group (2026-03-02 -> 2026-07-02), synthesized 2026-07-06.

lesson: Constant-currency (FX) rate reset is a large, legitimate ARR mover, not a logic bug. FY26->FY27 reset (~Feb 19) added +$95M EB (EUR -8.8%, GBP -3.8%, CHF -8.8%). Always rule out FX before treating a QoQ variance as a bug; announced '$X changes' often already include the reset.

Short-term contracts are annualized to 365 days, which writes ARR up; extensions then look like Expansion. Expect a few PvQ outliers; identify them via opportunity sub type. No ceiling logic exists (deemed immaterial).
ARR logic does NOT handle amendments (especially on short-term extensions). This causes FSE/ARR mismatches (Walmart FSE, DSW expansion). Known limitation - flag rather than treat as a new bug.

$0 ARR records exist INTENTIONALLY in Expansion/Contraction (for PvQ attribution and $0 extensions/opportunities). Do not remove them wholesale - only $0 records that neither start nor expire. They skew counts but not ARR/FSE/PvQ.

NRR/GRR lifetime filters are three ordered rules: (1) exclude M&A products until quarter 5 post-acquisition, (2) exclude accounts <12 months history, (3) exclude products <12 months history. Filter #3 wrongly dropped product churn/swaps in year 1 for tenured non-acquisition accounts - business decision (6/25) removed #3 for non-acquisition products. Acquisition quarter filter must be >4 (not >=4).

ACV and ARR will not always tie by segment: ARR consolidates at the AGREEMENT, so a 50/50 opportunity split across two segments (e.g. Partner + North America) defaults the whole agreement to one segment. Also ACV vs ARR category can diverge (a deal can be Add-On for ACV but Net Expansion for ARR).

Always state BOTH as_was_dates in any comparison (e.g. 2026-02-11 close vs 2026-05-11 current). ARR is a quarterly-released, restated dataset keyed on as_was_date; day-over-day changes between closes are expected.

As-Reported ARR (default dashboard view) excludes acquired businesses for periods before acquisition date; Pro-Forma includes them. Operationalized by is_acquired_sku / is_pre_acquisition, where is_pre_acquisition = is_acquired_sku AND agreement_start_date < acquisition_date. Prism/Adaptive (LRP) reads SOURCE tables directly and can show pre-acquisition rows ARR filters out (Paradox $123M Prism vs $18M Sigma).

lesson: ACV validation rule: the SKU-level breakdown MUST sum to the opportunity amount (opp.AMOUNT). A SKU decomposition that doesn't tie to the opp total is a defect - this is the single most common ACV bug class. Always assert sum(sku_acv) = opp_acv per opp when validating ACV models/overrides.
